# Session and state

Read on startup/resume or when establishing authoritative paths.

## Establish the boundary

1. Use the exact control-file or entry path supplied by the user. If only a workshop
   root is supplied, try its conventional `session.md`. If missing, ask for the exact
   path; do not scan the root, siblings, or version history.
2. Read the control file and only its explicit current-state/checkpoint references.
3. Establish run ID, neutral phase ID, status, accepted checkpoint, active package
   version, allowed paths, working-record destinations, and assistance policy.
4. Ask only for missing information essential to the next action. Do not demand a
   complete form before discussion. When admitting a package, read Package contract
   from the core skill; validate entry metadata without preloading sources.

Never infer release state from a filename. Keep future packages outside the facilitation
session and working directory when practical. Do not request a course map, instructor
solutions, designer skill, or full progression as extra context.

## Minimum control record

- Run/phase IDs; phase and integrity status; package ID/version.
- Exact current entry and accepted checkpoint paths.
- Released evidence IDs/paths; external technical research rules.
- Working-record locations; checkpoint destination; next-package drop location.
- Who can accept a checkpoint; participant/trainer roles if supplied.
- Known contamination, rule amendments, and open integrity questions.

Use neutral next-package IDs only when supplied. Do not invent the next phase's theme,
contents, or timing. Ask for a trainer-assigned identifier if necessary.

## Separate three state classes

| Class | Authority | Editing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Released source / accepted history | What was available or accepted then | Retain; append corrections |
| Current-state view | Derived index of current architecture, commitments, budgets | Update with links to authoritative entries |
| Alternatives / hypothetical branches | Exploratory, unaccepted | Revise freely; label |

Keep a small current-state view containing the current decision, next action, accepted
design/artifact versions, stakeholder promises, SLO/SLA status, negotiations, costs,
remaining capacity, assumptions, risks, debt, unknowns, released evidence, and checkpoint.

Do not create a separate file for every item. Start with a few Markdown records; split
when navigation requires it. Use stable IDs. Preserve primary sources and exact references;
summaries must not replace evidence. On resume, read the current view and checkpoint,
then follow only references relevant to the task. Do not reload the whole transcript.

## Check integrity

Compare checkpoint identity, accepted decisions, totals, and artifact versions with
their records. Inspect only referenced files. If an accepted item changed, a cost
vanished, or authoritative evidence is missing, identify the conflict and hold dependent
work. Do not restore from memory or silently overwrite records. Load Recovery and
debrief from the core skill. Let unrelated released-evidence discussion continue.
